doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Baritone, other horns and the Lincoln Center band
title: Baritone players he admires
summary: Harry Carney as his idol, plus Cecil Payne, Pepper Adams, Brignola, Cuber, Smulyan and Gerry Mulligan.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Of your contemporaries on the instrument these days, who do you feel are up there in the top league? I know that you’re fond of Ernie Caceres in his day.

Oh yeah, Ernie Caceres, and of course Harry Carney was always my idol. I really thought Harry Carney was the epitome of the sound of the baritone. I like other people. I like Cecil Payne, I’m very fond of Cecil Payne, and he’s a very good personal friend of mine. But I mean before that I was attracted to his playing tremendously, especially when he was at the height of his powers in the 50s and early 60s. Cecil’s approach to the baritone was just wonderful. But I like other people. I like Pepper a lot and I like Nick Brignola and Ronnie Cuber and Gary Smulyan and people like that playing today. And of course I loved Gerry Mulligan. Gerry was a good friend of mine too, and I’ve actually done some concerts, memorial concerts. We did one with the Lincoln Center Band at Lincoln Center. I went to Vienna and did one with Bob Brookmeyer and Lee Konitz. So that’s interesting too. We might do some more of that I don’t know.
